findings.evidence: Lie/Cotangent.lean:55-62 declare the local instances; Lie/Basic.lean:220 and :232 are the two overlapping global `LieAlgebra` instances that coincide at `B = R`. No other file in the repo declares a `local instance` that shadows an already-global instance (the other `attribute [local instance]` uses, e.g. `Comodule.dual`, are for genuinely non-global instances).
findings.fix: Delete both `local instance` blocks and let the file use the globally-resolved instances. If that fails to elaborate, the `B = R` overlap in `Lie/Basic.lean` is the real defect and must be resolved there (drop `instLieAlgebra` in favour of restriction along `Algebra R B`, or set explicit priorities) rather than pinned per-file.
findings.issue: The two `noncomputable local instance` declarations pin `Derivation.instLieRing`/`Derivation.instLieAlgebra` at `B = R`, and `cotangentDualLieEquiv` (line 78) is exported with those instances baked into its type. `Lie/Basic.lean` declares both `instLieAlgebra : LieAlgebra R (Derivation R A (CounitAlgebra R A B))` (line 220) and `instLieAlgebraCoefficients : LieAlgebra B (...)` (line 232), which overlap at `B = R`; default synthesis downstream picks the later one, not the pinned one. So the exported Lie equivalence is stated against an instance no consumer's `LieEquiv R _ (Derivation R H (CounitAlgebra R H R))` will synthesize, and composing it with the `LieHom`/`LieEquiv` API over `R` is a defeq-unification gamble rather than a syntactic match.

findings.evidence: Lie/Adjoint/Cotangent.lean:75-96 give `_one` (simp) and `_mul` (no simp) with no `_symm`/inverse lemma; `HopfAlgebra.points` is documented as "the bundled group of `A`-points" in PointsFunctor.lean:25.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem adjointLieEquiv_symm (A) (g) : (adjointLieEquiv A g).symm = adjointLieEquiv A g⁻¹`, and annotate `adjointLieEquiv_mul` with `@[simp]` for consistency with `adjointLieEquiv_one`.
findings.issue: `adjointLieEquiv` is presented as a group action by Lie automorphisms — `adjointLieEquiv_one` (line 77) and `adjointLieEquiv_mul` (line 89) are given — but the inverse law is missing: there is no `(adjointLieEquiv A g).symm = adjointLieEquiv A g⁻¹`. `HopfAlgebra.points A` is a bundled group (`PointsFunctor.lean:101`, `CommAlgCat R ⥤ GrpCat`), so `g⁻¹` is in scope and consumers cannot compute the inverse automorphism without re-deriving it from `_mul`/`_one`. Separately, `adjointLieEquiv_one` carries `@[simp]` while the parallel `adjointLieEquiv_mul` does not.

findings.evidence: Tangent/Cotangent.lean:148-154 (proof is `rw [algEquivSelf_apply, algEquivSelf_apply]; rfl`); the only external use is Lie/Cotangent.lean:146; `algEquivSelf_apply` is already `@[simp]` at Tangent/Basic.lean:99-107.
findings.fix: Keep it `private` and discharge the use site with `simp` after `Derivation.smul_apply`; if it must be public, move it into the `Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra` namespace next to `algEquivSelf_apply`/`algEquivSelf_symm_apply`.
findings.issue: `algEquivSelf_coeff_smul` is promoted from `private` to public solely to serve one `rw` in `Lie/Cotangent.lean:146`, but it is a trivial consequence of the existing `@[simp] Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf_apply` (`algEquivSelf R A B x = x`, Tangent/Basic.lean:100) — its own proof is two rewrites by that lemma plus `rfl`. It is also filed in `TauCeti.Derivation` although it says nothing about derivations; a user looking for `algEquivSelf` linearity will look in `Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra`.

summary: The Lie packaging is mostly well-characterized, but the exported `cotangentDualLieEquiv` is elaborated against file-local instance overrides, the `adjointLieEquiv` group-action API is missing the inverse law, and a private helper was un-privatized when the existing `@[simp]` lemma already discharges its one use.
